kept.claim: Adding the organization/BROKER_PUBLIC clause to the public LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate() changes IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate(), so in realms with organizations disabled a user's linked non-public organization broker is no longer shown on the login page.
kept.body:
## [GAP ANALYSIS] Changing `getLoginPredicate()` also changes login-page filtering for realms without organizations

**Severity:** LOW — a behavior change outside the cache that the PR description does not mention.

### The Problem

```java
public static Predicate<IdentityProviderModel> getLoginPredicate() {
    return ((Predicate<IdentityProviderModel>) Objects::nonNull)
            .and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))
            ...
```

This predicate is not only used by the new cache invalidation. `IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate()` (services/.../IdentityProviderBean.java:225-226) returns it directly, and `getFederatedIdentityProviders` filters the user's already-linked brokers with it (line 213).

### Theory / Proof

`FreeMarkerLoginFormsProvider` (line 482-486) uses the plain `IdentityProviderBean` when `ORGANIZATION` is disabled or `realm.isOrganizationsEnabled()` is false. In that mode `getLinkedBrokerAliases` returns the user's federated identities, including ones linked through an org-bound broker that is not public. Before this PR such a broker passed `federatedProviderPredicate()`. After it, the broker is filtered out. A user who re-authenticates (for example with `prompt=login`, or after identify-first) no longer sees the broker they are linked with, and because the set is non-empty, no realm brokers are offered either.

`OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean` already adds the same org/public clause itself (lines 86-96), so the new clause is redundant there and only changes the non-org path.

### What happens today vs. what will break

This only matters when a realm has org-linked IDPs but organizations are turned off for the realm (for example an admin switched the realm toggle off after setting orgs up). It is uncommon but reachable.

### Research

The SPI Javadoc for `LoginFilter` says it "contains all fields that are considered when deciding if a provider should be available for login". Callers treat it as the flag-based filter matching `getLoginSearchOptions()`, and that method was not extended.

### Recommendation

Keep the public predicate unchanged and put the org rule in the cache class:

```java
// InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider
private static final Predicate<IdentityProviderModel> LOGIN_CACHE_PREDICATE =
        getLoginPredicate().and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null
                || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)));
```

If the change is intended, document it and add a test for the organizations-disabled login page.
kept.evidence: IdentityProviderBean.java:213,225-226 filters the user's linked brokers with getLoginPredicate(). FreeMarkerLoginFormsProvider.java:482-486 uses the plain bean when orgs are disabled. A linked non-public org broker was shown before the PR and is filtered out after it, and the non-empty linked set prevents any fallback. OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.java:86-108 already applies the org/public check, so the new clause only changes the non-org path.

kept.claim: The cleanup registers testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove, a literal alias that never exists, so the 20 remaining IDPs created by testCacheIDPForLogin are never removed and leak into later tests in the realm.
kept.body:
## [ISSUE] Test cleanup removes a nonexistent IDP named "alias"

**Severity:** LOW — test hygiene. The created IDPs leak into other tests that count or list IDPs in the test realm.

### The Problem

```java
testRealm().identityProviders().create(idpRep).close();
getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);
```

This is at line 381 inside the loop, and again at line 425. The resource is resolved for the literal alias `"alias"`, not `idpRep.getAlias()`. None of the IDPs `idp-alias-0` through `idp-alias-20` is ever removed. Each queued cleanup calls `DELETE .../identity-provider/instances/alias`, which returns 404. Depending on how `TestCleanup` handles exceptions, that is either swallowed or makes cleanup noisy.

### Theory / Proof

`IdentityProvidersResource.get(String alias)` binds the path parameter when it is called, and the method reference captures that bound resource. The existing test at line 303 has the same copy-paste bug, and this PR copies it.

### What happens today vs. what will break

This passes today only if nothing else in the class counts IDPs or reuses the `idp-alias-*` names. Any test later in the same realm that creates `idp-alias-0` gets a 409 conflict, and assertions on IDP counts or login-page broker lists are off by 20.

### Research

Other organization tests in the same package use `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get(idpRep.getAlias())::remove)` or `RealmBuilder` managed resources.

### Recommendation

```java
String alias = "idp-alias-" + i;
idpRep.setAlias(alias);
...
testRealm().identityProviders().create(idpRep).close();
getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get(alias)::remove);
```

Apply the same fix at line 425 (`idp-alias-20`). Skip the cleanup for `idp-alias-1`, which the test removes explicitly.
kept.evidence: OrganizationCacheTest.java:381,425 register get("alias")::remove. TestCleanup.java:65-71 swallows the 404. isImportAfterEachMethod() is false (AbstractKeycloakTest.java:271), so the realm is shared by all test methods in the class and the IDPs leak into later tests. AbstractOrganizationTest.java:143 shows the correct pattern. The validator corrected the count: 20 IDPs leak, not 21, because idp-alias-1 is removed explicitly.
